notes.summary: Analysis of Variance (ANOVA, by R.A. Fisher) tests whether three or more group means are equal by splitting total variation into "between groups" and "within groups" parts and comparing them with an F-ratio.

concepts.title: One-way ANOVA
concepts.body:
• TSS = SSB (between / treatments) + SSW (within / error).
  • With k groups and N total observations: df between = k − 1, df within = N − k, df total = N − 1.
  • MSB = SSB/(k − 1), MSW = SSW/(N − k), F = MSB/MSW.
  • If F > table F, reject H0 that all means are equal.

concepts.title: Two-way ANOVA (one observation per cell)
concepts.body:
With r rows and c columns: df rows = r − 1, df columns = c − 1, df error = (r − 1)(c − 1), df total = rc − 1. TSS = SSR + SSC + SSE.
Assumptions of ANOVA: normal populations, equal variances (homoscedasticity), independent observations.

tips: Degrees of freedom add up just like sums of squares.
F is always non-negative; F close to 1 suggests no difference among means.
For two groups, one-way ANOVA F equals t².
traps: MSW uses N − k, not N − 1.
Total SS is not the sum of mean squares.
ANOVA tests equality of MEANS, though it does so by comparing variances.

questions.q: In analysis of variance, the test statistic used is:
questions.solution: ANOVA compares the between-group mean square with the within-group mean square; their ratio follows the F-distribution.

questions.q: In a one-way ANOVA with 4 treatments and 20 observations in all, the degrees of freedom for error (within) are:
questions.solution: df within = N − k = 20 − 4 = 16. (df between = 3, df total = 19.)

questions.q: One-way ANOVA: k = 4 groups, N = 24, SSB = 60, SSW = 120. The F-ratio is:

Three groups: A = {2, 4, 6}, B = {5, 7, 9}, C = {8, 10, 12}. The F-ratio for one-way ANOVA is:
questions.solution:
Group means: 4, 7, 10. Grand mean = 63/9 = 7.
SSB = 3[(4−7)² + (7−7)² + (10−7)²] = 3 × 18 = 54.
SSW: each group has deviations −2, 0, 2 ⇒ 8 per group ⇒ 24.
MSB = 54/2 = 27; MSW = 24/(9 − 3) = 4.
F = 27/4 = 6.75.
